PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: character-john-the-baptist-last-freed-before-resurrection-appearance
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Character guard: the row alone defines identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, hair, scars, costume, wounds, pose, and carried objects. Never turn a non-Jesus character into a Jesus lookalike.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
JOHN THE BAPTIST - LAST FREED BEFORE RESURRECTION — APPEARANCE: FOUR-VIEW IDENTITY, ANATOMY, COSTUME, AND CONTINUITY REFERENCE.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

John the Baptist as the last major named righteous soul freed in Hell's inner prison chamber immediately before the resurrection ascent—the forerunner who prepared the way and now sees the One he announced face to face. Photoreal live-action biblical epic character ingredients sheet of one continuous human identity locked across four panels: frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body standing, strict side profile, and rear-head/costume construction view. One face exists only on the front of the head; the rear panel shows only hair, neck, and garment construction with no second face, mask, or facial features on the back of the skull.

Identity and physique: adult Levantine man, age look late thirties to early forties but worn far beyond calendar years by dual imprisonment—first Herod's dark cell on earth, then the spiritual bondage of Hades. Height approximately five feet ten inches. Severely thin ascetic build: visible clavicles, lean corded forearms, sunken cheeks, sharp cheekbones, hollowed temples, and a narrow waist from long fasting and confinement; not skeletal caricature, still a living man with residual desert-prophet strength in shoulders and hands. Skin tone Mediterranean olive-brown, pale and dust-dulled from centuries in the chamber, with ashy grey film in pores and fine cracks of dried salt from old tears along the lower lids and cheek channels. No modern grooming; skin has realistic subsurface scattering under divine rim light, slight bluish cool shadow in recessed areas from residual hell torch ambience, warmer gold-amber catchlights where Christ's light reaches him.

Face and hair: long dark brown to near-black hair, thick but neglected, hanging past the shoulders in heavy matted ropes and irregular clumps, threaded with fine grey dust, grit, and a few pale ash flecks; hair completely covers the crown and continues down the nape so the rear view shows continuous dark coverage, not a bald spot or incomplete scalp. Long dark beard, similarly matted and uneven, parted slightly by breath and speech, dusted at the tips, with tear-tracks cutting cleaner darker paths through the powder on mustache edges and chin. Heavy brow ridge; deep-set dark brown eyes now ignited—prophetic fire of recognition and vindication, pupils catching warm golden specular highlights from divine intrusion, irises alive after dull captivity. Expression across panels: frontal three-quarter holds desperate hope turning to joyous recognition, mouth slightly parted as if about to cry out or bless, not a theatrical scream; profile shows the hawk-sharp ascetic nose and forward lean of a man who has waited a lifetime to see this King; full-body conveys relief after chains fall—weight redistributing onto bare or roughly shod feet, torso opening toward the source of light. Hands are clean of modern jewelry: long fingers, prominent knuckles, dry cracked cuticles, faint old callus from desert life, wrists and ankles showing pale chafed rings and slight indentations where hell chains have just released—subtle rawness and residual rust-colored grit, not gore-porn.

Costume—rough animal-skin garments (continuity lock with ward-john-the-baptist), strictly differentiated from Elijah's animal skins: John's covering is coarser desert-prophet camel-hair / rough hide aesthetic typical of the wilderness preacher, extremely worn from dual imprisonment, stripped to essentials with no staff, no bowl, no leather belt ornaments, no modern fastenings. Primary garment is a sleeveless or short-sleeved rough hide tunic hanging mid-calf to shin, uneven hem, stiff hair-side texture visible in raking light, irregular seams of sinew or crude gut stitching, patches of thinner worn leather at knees and hips, edges frayed and darkened with old sweat and dust. A second wrap of darker coarse hide or rough hairy fabric may cross one shoulder or cinch the waist in a simple twisted cord of leather strips—primitive, functional, never polished. No purple, no royal dye, no linen finery; palette is dry ochre-brown, soot-black, sun-bleached tan, and ashen grey. Bare feet or the suggestion of minimal ancient rawhide foot wraps only if needed for coherence—prefer bare dusty feet with dirt under toenails and pale chain marks at ankles. Rear costume panel must show continuous back of tunic, hair mass, shoulder blades faintly under hide, and the twisted cord knot if present.

Pose and story moment: the exact beat after mass chain release in Hell's vast inner chamber—thousands of pale souls free, pillars of black stone still present, blue torches not yet fully transformed, divine gold-white light flooding from Jesus's presence off-frame or as strong key from camera-left/above. John is newly unshackled; broken chain links may rest near his feet as environmental continuity, not as held props. In full-body he stands or half-steps forward, one or both hands reaching toward the divine light / Jesus with desperate hope and vindication after waiting—the forerunner recognizing the Lamb and the King. Portrait panels keep hands in frame when natural: open palms, reaching, not grasping weapons. No second character face in frame; Jesus is light direction and presence only if implied, never a competing portrait identity on this sheet.

Environment context (soft, not competing with character): deep hell fortress prison cavern—obsidian and black stone, residual cold blue torch spill ~2000K in background shadows, encroaching ethereal gold and pure white divine radiance ~6500K as key and rim, faint red underglow dying out. Thin smoke and floating ash motes in volumetric beams. Color grade: bruised crimson-black residual hell palette yielding to warm amber and sacred gold on skin and hair edges. Atmosphere: dust still falling from broken chain hardware; perfume of transformation only beginning; air that was poison now edged with warm light.

Lighting and camera language for production reference: physically coherent multi-panel lighting so identity reads as the same man under the same world light. Key: soft-hard divine golden-white from upper left or front-left, creating strong catchlights in eyes and translucent edges on matted hair strands. Fill: weak cool blue-torch bounce from environment so shadow side retains hell context without crushing blacks completely. Rim: thin pure white-gold edge along shoulder and hair silhouette separating him from dark stone. No neon, no lens brand text, no anachronistic gear. Think wide cinematic portrait optics feel—approximately 50–85mm portrait compression for face panels, slightly wider full-body for proportion honesty, shallow to moderate depth of field on portrait so background falls soft, full-body sharper environmental context. Aspect framing as clean multi-view reference panels without borders, captions, labels, UI, watermarks, logos, or readable text of any kind.

Texture and material fidelity: every strand of matted hair with dust particulate; hide pores and hair-side nap of animal skins; dry cracked lips with moisture only at inner edge if speaking; tear-salt crystallinity on cheeks; realistic eye moisture; hide translucency at thin worn edges; stone grit under nails; subtle subsurface life returning to skin as divine light hits him—the visual of a man who announced the Kingdom and now stands free at its victory.

Continuity locks (repeat for model adherence): same gaunt Levantine face, same matted dark hair covering full crown and rear head, same rough animal-skin desert-prophet garments with no accessories, same dual-imprisonment wear and chain chafe marks, same prophetic fire in dark eyes, same height and thin proportions across all four views. Differentiated from Elijah: thinner dual-prison gauntness, dust-and-tear matted hair rather than pure wild fire-prophet mane, coarser camel-hair/hide wilderness garment, no staff, expression of recognition and vindication toward Christ rather than isolated prophetic intensity alone. Photorealistic live-action biblical epic production still aesthetic—not illustration, not anime, not CGI cartoon, not fantasy superhero redesign. No modern objects, no logos, no text overlays, no watermarks, no borders, no captions. One human face only on the front of the head in every panel.
